regions.name: Kanata
regions.tagline: The Region of the Long Winter
regions.etymology: From kanata, the St. Lawrence Iroquoian word for "village" — the word that gave Canada its name.
regions.blurb: A vast northern region of boreal pine, shield rock and frozen coast. Trainers start among the maple groves of the south, climb the mining ranges, cross the cattle prairies, and finish their journey on the aurora-lit tundra where the ice legends nest.

sections.label: Maplewood Grove — Starters
sections.note: Professor Maple hands out one of three: a sapling, a lit branch, or a fledgling emperor.

sections.label: Route 1 — First Steps
sections.note: The bird, the beaver and the bugs every Kanatan trainer meets first.

sections.label: Aurora Flats
sections.note: Static crackles off the northern lights here, drawing anything that holds a charge.

sections.label: The Boreal Belt
sections.note: Endless black spruce and pine. Owls above, something much larger in the snow between the trunks.

sections.label: Shieldstone Range
sections.note: Old grey rock and older mine shafts. The compass needles here point at the Pokemon, not the pole.

sections.label: The Long Prairie
sections.note: Wheat, wool and a horizon that does not interrupt itself for anything.

sections.label: Karonto City & the Ravines
sections.note: The region's largest city: a lakefront, a needle you can see from an hour away, more construction cranes than anywhere on the continent, and a ravine system nobody ever managed to build over. Everything here has learned to live off people, and most of it is winning.

sections.label: The Great Lakes
sections.note: Freshwater inland seas, muskeg bogs, and the rivers the salmon climb every autumn.

sections.label: The Cold Atlantic
sections.note: Lobster traps, fog banks, and a lighthouse that has never once been switched off.

sections.label: The Treeline Tundra
sections.note: Past the last tree. Bears, caribou herds, pack ice, and the region's signature cold-dwellers.

sections.label: Northern Lights Sanctuary
sections.note: A single Eevee is gifted here. What the aurora makes of it is up to the aurora.

sections.label: The Shale Beds — Fossils
sections.note: A cliff of impossibly old sea creatures, and a badland of much newer, much larger ones.

sections.label: Summit Trial
sections.note: The region's pseudo-legendary, raised on the highest and coldest peaks.

sections.label: Legends of Kanata
sections.note: Three powers and a witness: the one above, the one in the cold, the one below the ice — and the forest that was here before all of them and expects to outlast them.

regions.name: Anahua
regions.tagline: The Region Where the Sun is Kept
regions.etymology: From Anáhuac, the Nahuatl name — roughly "land ringed by water" — for the highland valley at the heart of Mexico.
regions.blurb: A sun-hammered region of cactus flats, live volcanoes and green cenote country. Trainers begin in the jungle lowlands, cross the desert, climb the smoking sierra, and end among the glyph-carved tombs where the sun legend still roosts.

sections.label: Ceiba Village — Starters
sections.note: Professor Ceiba offers a vine, a singer, or a river-jaw.

sections.label: Route 1 — The Dry Wash
sections.note: The bird, the rodent and the bugs every Anahuan trainer meets first — including the ones that migrate here in their millions.

sections.label: Thunderhead Mesa
sections.note: The rain god's storms break over this mesa every afternoon in the wet season.

sections.label: The Cenote Caves
sections.note: Flooded limestone shafts, and the colonies that boil out of them at dusk.

sections.label: Obsidian Desert
sections.note: Burrows, serpents, cactus and bleached bone under a very large sky.

sections.label: Sunstone Flats
sections.note: Everything here turns to follow the sun, and two things here answer to the sky itself.

sections.label: The Smoking Sierra
sections.note: Three active cones, a lava flow, and air you can taste from the next valley over.

sections.label: Yucatl Jungle
sections.note: Canopy so thick the floor never dries. Watch the branches, not the path.

sections.label: The Floating Gardens
sections.note: Reed islands on a shallow lake. One resident is found nowhere else on earth; another never stops dancing.

sections.label: Tenoch City
sections.note: One of the largest cities on earth, sunk a little further into its old lakebed every year. Painted wall to wall, loud from before dawn, and fed entirely from the street.

sections.label: City of the Dead
sections.note: One night a year the marigold road opens, the candles are lit, and the residents come out to visit.

sections.label: The Glyph Temples
sections.note: Step pyramids covered in a script that will not hold still long enough to be read.

sections.label: The Great Arena
sections.note: Masks, ropes, and a crowd that can be heard three streets away — and next door, a stadium that holds a hundred thousand and has decided two World Cups. The region's two proudest traditions share a car park.

sections.label: The Turquoise Reef
sections.note: Warm shallows and a coral shelf that runs the length of the eastern coast.

sections.label: The Impact Crater — Fossils
sections.note: A ring of cenotes marks where something enormous once fell out of the sky and ended a world.

sections.label: Feathered Serpent Trial
sections.note: The region's pseudo-legendary, and the shape its oldest god is carved in.

sections.label: Legends of Anahua
sections.note: Three powers and a witness: the sun that dies and comes back, the serpent that rules the sky, the land that withholds the rain — and the small thing in the jungle that everything else descends from.

thematic.label: Thematic
thematic.blurb: Built on the region's real-world cultures, myths, stories, industries or institutions.

fauna.label: Animal / Fauna
fauna.blurb: Based on an animal or plant genuinely tied to the region.

stylistic.label: Stylistic
stylistic.blurb: Matches the region's design aesthetic — its landscape, palette and mood.

mechanics.label: Mechanics
mechanics.blurb: Fills a slot a Pokémon region needs: a starter, a route staple, type coverage, a fossil, a pseudo-legendary, a legendary.
